note: 'I shall not want' beside 'I have learned ... to be content'. Paul's word is want, in the same verse -- 'I am not saying this out of need' (Phil 4:11) -- which is the shared term and the only one. The difference is worth seeing: the psalm states not wanting as a condition, Paul as something he had to learn.

'I shall not want' (Ps 23:1) and 'my God will supply all your needs' (Phil 4:19) -- the same claim from the two ends, one as what is not lacked and one as what is provided. No shared wording, and neither text refers to the other, so the pairing is the graph's.

**Three verses put the anointing and the Spirit in one sentence.** 'Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward' (1Sam 16:13). 'The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me, because the LORD has anointed Me' (Isa 61:1). Luke 4:18 quotes Isaiah word for word at the opening of the ministry.

In Samuel the anointing comes first and the Spirit follows; in Isaiah the Spirit is stated first and the anointing is the reason. Ps 23:5 has the word and neither -- which is what makes it a different use rather than a fourth instance.
'the horn of oil and anointed him' (1Sam 16:13); 'You anoint my head with oil' (Ps 23:5).

'reviving the soul' (Ps 19:7) and 'He restores my soul' (Ps 23:3). The soul is the shared word and the verbs are close without being the same. Two psalms, no cross-reference between them, so the join is the graph's -- and worth having, since one attributes the restoring to the shepherd and the other to the law.
'The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.' (Ps 23:1) -- one verse, two clauses.
v5 of the same psalm, and the verse where the shepherd becomes a host.

'I will fear no evil, for You are with me' (Ps 23:4) and 'Do not fear, for I am with you' (Isa 41:10). Both give the same two things in the same order -- the fear denied, and the presence as its reason -- one in the first person and one in the second. Neither cites the other.

'I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever' (Ps 23:6) and 'In My Father’s house are many rooms ... I go to prepare a place for you' (John 14:2). House is the shared word. The psalm ends in the house; the gospel has someone leaving to make room in it.
